newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras shoves Brazil shrs lower, trade volatile.
newsitem.headline: Telebras shoves Brazil shrs lower, trade volatile.

text.p: Brazilian stocks extended losses, diving 5.2 percent in seesaw trade mid-afternoon on speculative selling of bellwether Telebras, traders and analysts said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active shares was down at 11,984 points at 1545 local time/1845 GMT in rising volume of 1.07 billion reais ($990 million).

Telebras, whose preferred stock was down 7.76 percent percent at 148.50 reais, was weighed down by local wire reports that it would have to begin lowering the cost of its services as of 1998 to face competition with private sector.

According to local wire reports, Telebras director Daltron Magalhaes said the firm would have to adapt itself to a competitive environment, indicating that further rate hikes were unlikely to take place, particularly for commercial users.
No Telebras officials were immediately available for comment on the report.
The market opened up Thursday, but seesawed in the morning before trading slightly lower at midday. Stocks extended losses after traders returned from lunch.

The market was also rattled earlier this week by comments by Communications Minister Sergio Motta criticizing Central Bank Foreign Affairs director Gustavo Franco for putting economic stability above economic development. His criticism suggested a government split on economic policy.
Vidigal said that "without reports like that, volatility could ease", adding that the market has not fully recovered from its recent turbulence despite Wednesday's surge.
Other blue chips also traded lower. Federal power holding Eletrobras was down 5.95 percent at 616 reais.
